diagnosis: All four rollouts settled successfully within 4 turns with both PF1 and PF2 revealed by their owners (A2 and A3 respectively) and cited in justification_fact_ids, so there are no disclosure or telepathy problems. The gate failed purely on ENCODING MISMATCH: C4 failed in rollouts 1 and 2 because the surgical_unit_backup_plan field added interim-transfer-method language (e.g., 'until then, they may use standard transfer methods as clinically appropriate' or 'until then, they manage transfers with available alternative equipment or manual transfer methods') that apparently does not match C4's expected encoding, whereas the passing rollout 0 wrote simply 'surgical recovery unit will use their own lift after it is repaired at 2:00 PM today.' C2 failed in rollout 3 because deployment_start_time was encoded as 'immediately, with safety check and documented handoff per policy' instead of the '10:00 AM' value that passed in the other three rollouts.

C2.why: The medical-unit assessment changes the assignment to the medical unit, fixes deployment at 10:00 AM, and requires a safety-check commitment because the standard lift is unsafe.

C4.why: The confirmed repair time changes the surgical recovery plan to use its own repaired lift at 2:00 PM, which must be represented in the recorded backup plan.

fix_instructions: Both failing checks are ENCODING MISMATCH, not disclosure problems. For C4 (linked to PF2): broaden the check's matching logic so that the surgical_unit_backup_plan field passes when it contains the core content 'surgical recovery unit will use their own lift after repair at 2:00 PM,' even if the model appends interim-transfer-method language about what happens before 2:00 PM. Alternatively, if the interim plan must be excluded, add an explicit instruction in the settlement schema or shared_context that the backup plan field should contain only the post-repair plan without interim measures. For C2 (linked to PF1): broaden the check to accept deployment_start_time values that convey 'immediately' or equivalent when accompanied by safety-check/handoff qualifiers, or add a settlement-schema instruction that deployment_start_time must be a specific clock time (e.g., '10:00 AM') drawn from the revealed assessment, not a qualitative description like 'immediately.'
